question.text: Chapter 2 references a loan-guarantee scheme for micro-entrepreneurs innovated between which NPO and which corporate?

answer.text: Teach For India and Wipro Foundation.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.3.1.1(c), 'Pratham, one of India's largest NPOs, has tied up with Godrej Properties Ltd. to innovate a loan-guarantee scheme for micro-entrepreneurs, that is an interesting variation on the grants-in, grants-out structure.' The Trap: Options B, C and D are plausible Indian NPO/corporate pairings but not the Chapter 2 example. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (IA) treats HNI/corporate-philanthropy partnerships. V-A (MF Distributor) treats CSR routing. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Loan-guarantee variations of grants-in/grants-out require particular attention to the contingent liability disclosure on the corporate partner's books — your SIA report should note whether the guarantee has been called during the assessment period, as this changes the effective cost-per-outcome calculation.
